title: Interval training's best-supported effect is on lean mass, not fat: thirty-six trials, graded [trials, grade_ffm, grade_bf]
teaser: Across thirty-six randomized trials in adults, interval training reduced body fat percentage by 1.53 points. [trials, bf_all] In the same adults, it raised fat-free mass by 0.51 kg. [trials, ffm_all] The fat result is graded low certainty. [grade_bf] The lean-mass result is graded high, and it hangs on a single trial. [grade_ffm, ffm_loo]
hook: Interval training is sold on fat loss. [-] Pool the trials, rate how far each result can be trusted, and the order flips. [grade_ffm, grade_bf]
populationPanel: Who was studied: 1,130 adults with a mean age of 26.27 years, across thirty-six randomized trials lasting 3 to 15 weeks. [sample, trials] Most were inactive and overweight or obese, so the findings describe that group best. [lim_population] Children, teenagers and people with a known disease were left out. [excluded]

card.question: Does interval training change your body fat and lean mass? [trials]
card.headline: Fat-free mass +0.51 kg; [ffm_all] fat mass −1.86 kg; [fm_all] both vs no exercise, trials pooled. [trials]
card.support: Fat-free mass is everything in the body that is not fat. [ffm_all]

glance.alt: Three rows, surest evidence first: fat-free mass, fat, then body fat share. Beside them, the order it is usually sold in, fat loss first. Each row has its own scale and a line for no change. [ffm_all, fm_all, bf_all, grade_ffm, grade_fm, grade_bf]
glance.note: Ranges from the pooled trials. Members can try it with their own training inside. [-]

paragraphs: Picture your weight as two piles on one scale. [concept:fat-free-mass] One pile is fat; the other is everything else: muscle, bone, organs, blood and water. [concept:fat-free-mass] A bathroom scale reads only the two together. [concept:fat-free-mass] The second pile has a name: fat-free mass. [ffm_all]
Interval training means bursts of hard work with rests between them. [recipe]

In these trials, interval training moved the two piles in opposite directions. [fm_all, ffm_all] Compared with no exercise, the fat pile shrank by 1.86 kg on average, and the other pile grew by 0.51 kg. [fm_all, ffm_all]
So a bathroom scale would show less than what changed underneath. [fm_all, ffm_all]

figure.headline: The scale weighs two things. [-] In these trials, interval training moved them in opposite directions. [fm_all, ffm_all]
figure.caption: Dotted: a sketch of the idea, not data. [-] Orange words: what the pooled trials measured. [fm_all, ffm_all] Dashed: the pattern the authors found more effective. [recipe]
figure.alt: Two panels, before and after 3 to 15 weeks of training, each with a standing outline beside two stacked blocks: fat below, everything else above. [trials] After training, the fat block is marked less, on average, and the other block a little more, on average. [fm_all, ffm_all] The blocks are drawn the same size in both panels, because the paper gives no sizes. [-] Below, two strips show two ways to build a session: short hard bursts with short easy rests, and long bursts with long still rests. [ffm_le60, ffm_rest_le90, ffm_active] The authors found the first pattern more effective. [recipe]

params.title: Fat and fat-free mass, before and after interval training
params.why: The trials did not test why.

recipe.words: The authors found the first pattern more effective.

paragraphs: The trials compared interval training with no exercise, for 3 to 15 weeks. [trials] Then the authors rated how far they could trust each result. [grade_ffm] Fat-free mass rated high, fat mass moderate and body fat percentage low. [grade_ffm, grade_fm, grade_bf]

Some settings kept coming out ahead. [recipe] More than 8 weeks, three sessions a week, bursts under 60 seconds, and rests of 90 seconds or less, spent moving. [recipe] These leads come from comparing groups of trials, not from testing one setting against another. [subgroups]
For fat-free mass, only cycling showed a clear gain; running did not. [ffm_cycling, ffm_only_cycling]

figure.headline: Sold on fat loss. [-] The surest result is that fat-free mass held up. [ffm_all, grade_ffm]
figure.caption: Compared with people who did no training. [ffm_all, fm_all, bf_all] Mostly inactive adults carrying extra weight. [lim_population]
figure.alt: Three rows, surest evidence first. [grade_ffm, grade_fm, grade_bf] Fat-free mass: 0.51 kg more, strong evidence. [ffm_all] Fat: 1.86 kg less, decent evidence. [fm_all] Body fat share: 1.53 points less, early evidence. [bf_all] With one trial left out, the fat-free-mass range crosses no change. [ffm_loo, lim_loo]

params.title: What thirty-six trials found, surest first

sensitivity.crosses: and the range crosses no change.

audit.effect: Fat-free mass: 0.51 kg more than with no exercise, pooled across the trials. [ffm_all] Fat mass: 1.86 kg less. [fm_all] Body fat percentage: 1.53 points less. [bf_all]
audit.weakEnd: The 95% confidence interval for fat-free mass runs from 0.06 kg to 0.95 kg. [ffm_all] At its weak end, 0.06 kg is an amount no bathroom scale would register. [ffm_all] High certainty means the trials agree that the average is above zero, not that it is big. [grade_ffm, ffm_no_het]
limitations: Most trials enrolled inactive adults who were overweight or obese. [lim_population] People who already train may respond differently. [lim_population]
The trials disagreed with one another, most of all on body fat percentage, which is why the authors graded it low. [lim_heterogeneity, grade_bf]
The trials measured body composition in different ways, from skinfold calipers to DEXA scans. [lim_methods]
Take one trial out and the fat-free-mass result is no longer clear. [lim_loo]
audit.missed: Leave that trial out and the estimate becomes 0.46 kg lost, ranging from 1.38 kg lost to 0.44 kg gained. [ffm_loo] So the best-graded result also rests on a single study. [ffm_loo, grade_ffm]
more: Cycling’s fat-free-mass gain was 0.63 kg (95% CI 0.17 to 1.09). [ffm_cycling]
Overground running showed the widest drop in body fat percentage, 2.80 points (95% CI 3.89 to 1.71), on the outcome graded low. [bf_overground, grade_bf]
Treadmill running showed no clear difference in fat mass: from 2.82 kg lost to 0.62 kg gained. [fm_treadmill]
An earlier pooled analysis found no clear effect of cycling on fat mass in overweight and obese adults. [wewege]
Heavier bodies load the joints differently when running, one reason cycling may suit some people. [joints]

glossary.plain: Exercise in bursts of hard work, with rests between them.
Chance decided who did the training and who did not, not the researchers.

words.alt: Two stacked blocks beside a standing outline: a sketch of the body as a fat pile and a pile of everything else. The blocks are the same size in both panels; their sizes are not data.

labels.free: Fat-free mass: everything else (muscle, bone, water)

takeaways: If lean mass is the aim, the supported combination in these trials was cycling intervals, three sessions a week, for more than 8 weeks. [ffm_cycling, ffm_3wk, ffm_over8]
Keep work bursts to 60 seconds or less: longer bursts showed no clear gain in fat-free mass, with an interval from 2.28 kg lost to 0.57 kg gained. [ffm_le60, ffm_gt60]
Keep moving during the rest. [ffm_active] Standing still between bursts showed no clear gain in fat-free mass. [ffm_passive]
Two sessions a week did not clearly change body fat percentage; three did. [bf_2wk, bf_3wk]

slides.heading: Intervals are sold on fat loss. Thirty-six trials, graded, tell it differently. [trials, grade_bf, grade_ffm]
What changed [-]
slides.body: In adults, interval training reduced body fat percentage by 1.53 points and raised fat-free mass by 0.51 kg, compared with no exercise. [bf_all, ffm_all]

slides.heading: The grades run backwards [-]
slides.body: Certainty for the lean-mass result: high. [grade_ffm] For body fat percentage: low. [grade_bf] The claim that gets the attention has the weaker evidence. [grade_bf, grade_ffm]

slides.heading: And the strong one is fragile [-]
slides.body: Remove a single trial and the lean-mass gain becomes 0.46 kg lost, with an interval from 1.38 kg lost to 0.44 kg gained. [ffm_loo]

slides.heading: Who this describes [-]
slides.body: 1,130 adults in trials of 3 to 15 weeks, most of them inactive and overweight or obese. [sample, trials, lim_population]

slides.heading: What to hold loosely [-]
slides.body: The trials disagreed with each other on body fat, and measured it with different tools. [lim_heterogeneity, lim_methods]

carousel.caption: Thirty-six randomized trials of interval training in adults, pooled and graded. [trials] Body fat percentage fell by 1.53 points, at low certainty. [bf_all, grade_bf] Fat-free mass rose by 0.51 kg, at high certainty, though the result depends on one trial. [ffm_all, grade_ffm, ffm_loo] Full read and simulator at the link in bio. [-]
